passage:
Hi Sarah and David,

I'm reaching out with some unexpected news regarding your wedding at the "Lakeside Pavilion" next month. I received a call this morning from the Parks Department informing me that due to a major water main break and subsequent soil erosion, the Pavilion and the surrounding lawn area have been deemed unsafe for public events and will be closed for emergency repairs until October.

I know this is incredibly stressful, especially with only four weeks to go, but please don't panic! My team and I have spent the last six hours on the phone, and I have secured a fantastic alternative for you: The "Glass Conservatory" at the Botanical Gardens. The best part is that they have your exact date (September 15) available due to a recent cancellation.

The Conservatory is actually a slight upgrade—it's fully climate-controlled, so we don't have to worry about the September heat, and the indoor floral displays are stunning, which will save us money on your additional flower arrangements. I've already spoken to your caterer and the florist, and both have confirmed they can move their setup to the new location without any extra fees.

I have already drafted a revised floor plan for the Conservatory that keeps your "circular seating" vision for the ceremony. The only minor change is that the parking lot is a bit further from the entrance, so I'm going to hire two additional golf-cart shuttles to transport your older guests from the gate to the front doors. I'll cover the cost of these shuttles myself as a gesture of goodwill for the late-night stress!

Could you please take a look at the photos of the Conservatory I've attached and let me know if you're okay with this switch? Once you give me the green light, I'll handle all the logistics of notifying your guests via a digital "Change of Venue" card.

We're going to make sure your day is still absolutely perfect!

Best,
Clara, Clara Simmons Events
